name: second compaction plus isolated post-publication GC interruption/retry result

gc_fixture.scope: isolated redundant loose copies only; authoritative tx event graph was not deleted
gc_fixture.first_pass: fresh compact authority read; deleted fixture A with expected blob; intentionally stopped before B
gc_fixture.retry: fresh compact authority read; A returned 404 and was treated as already-collected success; B still matched the packed body/blob and was deleted with its fresh known blob
gc_fixture.duplicate_retry: fresh compact authority unchanged; both fixture paths returned 404; terminal DONE_NOOP with no deletion attempt

design_revision.before: Compaction publication had been exercised but post-publication loose-copy GC interruption/retry remained untested.
design_revision.after: For redundant role-local copies with stable queryable paths, GC is restart-safe when publication is revalidated before each deletion, missing means already collected, existing content must equal the packed authoritative body, and deletion uses the observed blob SHA. Interruption after one delete and a duplicate retry both converge without touching authoritative tx events.

scope_limits: This proves only the bounded role-local GitHub text fixture with queryable identities and CAS/readback; it is not exactly-once semantics for opaque non-idempotent external effects.
The repository commit history still retains deleted fixture objects historically; the test is about current-tree reachability and retry semantics, not physical storage erasure.
No hosted runner, external object store, LFS, package/artifact quota, or richer/manual execution mode was used.
next_frontier: Define a small arithmetic/dataflow proof-carrying certificate language with explicit unsupported-operation rejection and negative controls.
Classify authorized connector writes by natural idempotence, caller-stable idempotency key, or stable queryable identity; keep opaque non-idempotent effects hard-gated.

Extend compaction proof with deterministic segment-boundary conflict fixture: stale planned segment after a competing compact-head CAS must reconstruct and recompute rather than publish stale boundaries.
